comments.text:
This conversation is ridiculous. Chagosian people/culture is not a thing. Those people are from all over Indian ocean territory. They were brought to the archipelago by Europeans and spent 150 years there. They managed to build some shacks for shelter (probably with the assistance of Europeans) and come up with a few dances. One can barely call it a culture. When the British came back to the archipelago in the 50s, those people still had no government structure. They are glorified survivolists.

Empires throughout history had expansion campaigns. They gain and lose territories. Whoever or whatever nation had a claim for the Chago Archipelago before the British conquest, they lost it. It is very generous for Great Britain to give back some of those islands and territories. It is ludacrious to demand the archipelago that you lost hundreds of years ago.

comments.author: @eastcoast_pete
comments.text: Diego Garcia is often called America's unsinkable aircraft carrier in the Indian Ocean.  As Geoff mentioned in his introduction, it's location makes it prime strategic real estate.  The Chagos islands are a great example for the three things that matter most in  real estate: " location, location, location". The UK would have  been glad to get Chagos and the associated (for the UK) embarrassing history off its plate.  The BIOT exists because the US needed a sort-of legal way for its military to stay and use the islands. While the exact motives for the US's change of opinion regarding the eventual transfer of the BIOT (initially in favor of a coordinated handover of the islands, now vehemently opposed) were never stated, it's clear that the ever-increasing presence of China in the Indian Ocean and in Africa  had a lot to do with it.
